battle.name: 隋平李英林叛亂
battle.theater: 並州晉陽城與汾水上游
battle.brief: 開皇二十年（600）冬，並州人李英林在晉陽起兵反隋，據城拒命，直撼北方軍防樞紐。隋廷詔令並州郡兵與京師宿衛合討，數月內事平，李英林伏誅，部曲家屬分置。記載雖少，顯示隋文帝整飭北周舊軍功集團後並州軍府人心不穩；卡面羅馬短劍不在此戰場上，可對照者為隋軍環首刀與長槊。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 這場衝突並非國與國之間的戰爭，而是隋朝開皇末年發生在北方軍鎮內部的一場叛亂，兩方都是隋朝的編制內力量，這一點必須先說清楚。叛亂的一方是並州（治晉陽，今山西太原）軍府體系中的武人李英林與其追隨者：李英林是並州軍府中的一名武將，在北周至隋的軍府序列中歷任基層職銜，家世與籍貫在流傳的記載裡多已模糊；開皇年間北周留下的舊軍功集團受到清算與改編，他所屬的那一層軍官、屯田軍戶與城郊豪族部曲因此受到牽動，事起之後以晉陽城為依託聚眾拒命，兵鋒所向是州郡的倉庫、馬場與屯田莊。鎮壓的一方是隋朝中央與並州官署的合體：皇帝自長安、洛陽兩端下詔，並州總管府、太原郡與晉陽縣的官軍先奉詔結集自保，宿衛軍與行軍總管再自京師及河北道北上接應。整個過程的指揮鏈條是「兵部—總管府—郡縣—校尉—隊長」一類的府兵制結構，州郡兵、宿衛、屯田軍戶與臨時糾集的鄉勇並行存在。叛軍並非外敵，沒有任何外部勢力介入，隋廷也沒有因此與他國開戰；這是一場內部秩序崩解後被迅速壓平的事件，卻牽動了北方邊防體系最敏感的一段神經。
countriesEn: The clash was not a war between states but a rebellion inside the military-administrative system of the Sui, in the last years of the Kaihuang era, and both sides consisted of men formally enrolled in Sui institutions. That point has to be made first. The rebel side was the arms-man Li Yinglin of Bingzhou (seat at Jinyang, present-day Taiyuan in Shanxi) together with those who followed him. Li was a soldier in the Bingzhou commandery office, holding junior posts in the military offices of the Northern Zhou and the Sui in turn; his family background and precise origin are blurred in the transmitted record. During the Kaihuang years the old Northern Zhou meritocracy was purged and reorganised, and the layer of junior officers, military-farm households and local clan followers to which he belonged was itself implicated. Once the rising began he made Jinyang city his base, gathered a following there and refused the state's orders, his armed strength aimed at the prefectural granaries, the horse pastures and the military farms of the region. The side that suppressed him was a compound of the central court and Bingzhou's own offices: the emperor issued the edicts from Chang'an and Luoyang; the troops of the Bingzhou zongguan office, of Taiyuan commandery and of Jinyang county first mustered on the strength of the imperial order to secure themselves; the palace guards and the marching commanders then came north from the capital and from the Hedong circuit. The chain of command was the fubing structure: ministry of war, zongguan office, commandery and county, then company commanders and file leaders, with prefectural troops, palace guards, military-farm households and hastily raised local auxiliaries all existing side by side. The rebels were not a foreign enemy, no outside power intervened, and the Sui did not go to war with any other regime over this. It was an internal breakdown of order put down quickly, and it still touched the most sensitive nerve of the northern frontier system.
people: 留下的名字不多，而最完整的一筆人物記載反而來自一名女子。《隋書·列女傳》記並州官眷樊氏為李英林之妻：叛亂事發後，朝廷以詔書責問其夫起兵之由，樊氏上表自白，陳述丈夫本無反心、其所以起事出於被逼迫與被讒言，並說明自己曾力勸不聽、未能阻止，表中措辭不卑不亢，把朝廷的賞罰之意與自身的處境一層層辨明。隋文帝讀了這份表章，對樊氏的持守有所稱許，下詔就其家眷作了寬免與褒獎之處置。這段記敘是本事件在傳世文獻中唯一保留下來的細節，也說明叛亂牽連的不只是軍將本人，還有留在城中的家眷。男性方面，李英林之外的並州官員姓名多已散失，記載裡只剩「奉詔討平」這類無名的執行者。隋文帝楊堅是全案的決策者，此時他正同時收拾北邊的邊患與內政，討、撫、誅、赦的分寸都由他定奪。開皇九年受封晉王、鎮守並州的晉王楊廣，開皇二十年仍在晉陽任上，叛亂就發生在他被召還京的那一年；秦王李世民則於開皇十九年前後撰《晉祠銘》刻於城南晉祠，追述高祖在太原一帶的軍旅舊事——叛亂前一年，晉陽正是天子文治的聚光燈下。
peopleEn: Few names survive, and the most complete personal record of the affair comes from a woman. The History of Sui, in its section on exemplary women, records Lady Fan, the wife of Li Yinglin, a woman of the Bingzhou officer corps. After the rising became known, the court questioned her by edict about her husband's reasons for taking arms; she submitted a memorial in her own defence, stating that her husband had never meant to rebel, that his taking arms was the result of coercion and slander, and that she had urged him and failed to stop him. The document argued her own conduct without servility or arrogance, weighing the court's purposes of reward and punishment against her own predicament layer by layer. The Wen emperor read the memorial, found something in Lady Fan's constancy that he approved of, and issued an edict sparing her household and commending her. This passage is the only particular detail the event has left in the transmitted record, and it shows that the rebellion reached beyond the rebel general to the families left inside the city. On the male side, almost none of the Bingzhou officers who took part survive by name; the record keeps only anonymous executors of the will to suppress the rising. The Wen emperor Yang Jian was the decision-maker throughout, at a moment when he was busy at once with the northern frontier and with domestic administration, and he fixed the measure of the edicts to punish, to pardon and to settle the matter. The Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, had been enfeoffed as Prince of Jin in the ninth year of Kaihuang and stationed at Bingzhou, and he was still holding that post in the twentieth year, the very year in which the rising broke out and in which he was summoned back to the capital. Prince Qin Li Shimin, for his part, composed the Jinci Inscription at the Jinci temple south of the city around the nineteenth year of Kaihuang, recalling the military exploits of the high ancestor around Taiyuan. A year before the rebellion, Jinyang stood under the full glare of the court's attention.
kits: 卡面上的羅馬短劍是羅馬軍團的標準制式配備：全長約六十至七十公分，雙刃、中脊，握柄多為木或骨質纏皮，柄頭作球形，全器約一公斤上下，通體無護手。它在體系中的位置很清楚——不是砍劈的兵器，而是大盾手在盾牆合攏、最後一步時用來刺穿的工具；配合的是半圓或橢圓形的大盾與重標槍，短兵相接時士兵先靠盾緣頂住敵方的刺與砍，再從盾後探身刺擊，劍是這套動作的最後一環。落到開皇二十年晉陽城下的隋軍，這套邏輯要換成另一副樣貌：近身兵器是環首直刃刀，刀身直脊直刃、單面開鋒、柄端作圓環，山西、河北出土的北周至隋唐刀環即是此制；雙刃的劍在隋代更多作為儀飾佩用，實戰上讓位於刀與長槊、標槊。防護上，隋軍步兵著明光鎧與札甲、戴兜鍪、持棗木或柳葉形盾，弩手用臂弩與蹶張弩，弓用角弓與木弓，槊、矛與鏑槍補上長兵器的距離；騎兵在開皇年間已有裝備馬甲的具裝騎兵，但數量有限，多充中軍精銳。攻城與守城器械齊備：撞車、雲梯、可焚城角的攻城車、可拋射石塊的投石機（舊志所謂發石機、霹靂車一類），以及火藥投射物——《隋書·西域傳》所記的突火槍與火藥箭，守城一方未必全備，卻說明六世紀末的隋軍已把火藥用於戰場。糧秣靠軍屯與屯田供給，牛車與驢隊負責運轉，馬匹來自河西走廊引進的良馬與各處馬場。
kitsEn: The gladius on the card face was standard issue in the Roman legions: sixty to seventy centimetres long, double-edged with a central ridge, the grip usually of wood or bone wrapped in leather, the pommel spherical, the whole weapon about a kilogram in weight, and with no crossguard at all. Its place in the system is clear. It is not a chopping weapon but the tool of a shieldman for the final thrust when the shield wall closes up; it works together with the large semicircular or oval scutum and the heavy pilum, and in close combat the soldier first braced the enemy's cuts and thrusts against the edge of his shield and then reached out from behind it to stab. The sword was the last link in that sequence. What stood in front of the Sui army below the walls of Jinyang in the twentieth year of Kaihuang was a different set of habits. The close-combat arm was the ring-pommel dao, a straight single-edged blade with a straight spine and a ring at the pommel; the straight-bladed ring-pommel knives excavated from Shanxi and Hebei in the Northern Zhou, Sui and Tang periods are of this pattern. The double-edged sword in the Sui was more often a piece of ceremonial wear, and on the field it gave way to the dao, the long shao and the biao spear. For protection, Sui infantry wore Mingguang plate and lamellar armour and steel helmets, carried jujube-wood or willow-leaf shields, and used arm bows and the powerful crossbow held by the foot; bows of horn and wood, spears, halberds and lance-and-dart weapons supplied the reach of the longer weapons. Mounted troops in the Kaihuang years already included armoured lancers, but in small numbers, mostly as an elite of the centre. Siege and defence equipment was complete: battering rams, scaling ladders, siege towers able to set fire to a corner of the wall, stone-throwers of the kind the old records call the fashi ji, and pyrotechnic projectors such as the tuohuo qiang and the gunpowder arrows described in the western regions chapter of the History of Sui; the defenders need not have had all of these, yet the point stands that by the end of the sixth century the Sui army already used gunpowder on the field. Supply came from military farms and agricultural colonies, with ox-carts and mule trains doing the hauling, and the horses were the good stock of the Hexi corridor and of the pastures nearer home.
tactics: 叛軍的作法是守城：李英林既據晉陽，就以城垣、甕城與城門為核心，城外結寨以納歸附的屯田軍戶與鄉里民壯，取糧於州郡倉庫與周遭莊園，控制汾水一線的渡口與通向河北洛陽的道路，靠城固守而不輕率出擊。隋廷的處置則是典型的「先斷後打」：詔書到州郡，命郡兵與縣兵就地結集，封鎖城郊道路與糧道，使叛軍不得外出劫掠；同時自京師宿衛與河北道調兵北上，騎兵先行，負責遮斷叛軍北面與突厥方面的聯繫、掃清城外的援手與散兵，再由步卒與攻具接續。城下的攻擊分兩種可能：或是憑夜襲與內應破門，或是以投石機與火箭壓制城上守軍，再用雲梯、撞車與攻城車附著；招撫與離間則貫穿其間——一旦叛軍部眾得知朝廷已調大軍至而罪及首惡者，死守的意願便會鬆動。與卡面對照更有意思：羅馬軍團靠三列縱深與大盾組成的盾牆，一步一步把戰線往前推，短劍只在盾牆合攏的一刻出手；隋軍的會戰樣式更倚重騎兵迂迴與弩箭、投石、火藥的火力先行，靠近城垣的最後一段才換上環首刀與長槊硬碰。
tacticsEn: The rebels fought as a garrison. With Jinyang in their hands they made the wall, the barbican and the gates the core of the position, raised stockades outside the city to absorb the military-farm households and local men who came in, drew grain from the prefectural stores and from the estates around the city, held the fords along the Fen and the roads towards Hedong and Luoyang, and on the whole stayed inside their walls rather than taking risks in the open. The court's response followed the classic pattern of cutting the enemy off first and beating him afterwards. The edict went out to the commanderies and counties, ordering the prefectural and county troops to muster on the spot and to close the roads and the supply lines around the city so that the rebels could not go out to forage; at the same time troops were drawn from the palace guards and from the Hedong circuit, cavalry first, to sever any link the rebels might have to the Turks on the north and to clear the field of auxiliaries and scattered bands, with infantry and siege equipment following. Two kinds of assault were possible at the wall: a night attack with help from within, or a preliminary barrage from the stone-throwers and fire-arrows to pin the defenders on the wall, followed by ladders, rams and siege towers pushed against the masonry. Between these ran inducement and division, for once the rank and file of the rebels learned that great bodies of imperial troops were coming and that the leaders alone would answer for the crime, the will to hold out to the death would weaken. The contrast with the card is instructive. The Roman legion advanced on the momentum of a triple line, its scuta locked into a moving wall, and the gladius came out only at the moment that wall closed. The Sui scheme of battle leaned instead on cavalry movement and on the fire of bolts, stones and gunpowder delivered first, and only the last stretch against the wall was settled with the ring-pommel dao and the long spears.
data: 留下數字的地方不多，可核的多是地理與制度：開皇二十年即西元600年，隋文帝自581年受禪稱帝到604年崩，在位已近二十年，開皇也是他最後的年號。晉陽在今山西太原市一帶，約在北緯三十七點八七度、東經一百一十二點五五度，汾河自北而來繞城西折南，晉祠在城南二十里許，合今約十公里。晉陽到東都洛陽直線約三百六十公里，到京師長安直線約五百公里；沿隋道經蒲坂、河東再折華山入京師，實際行程約一千四五百里，折合七百公里上下，意味著自京師調兵即便全速也要旬月。《隋書·地理志》所載並州太原郡為三萬餘戶、近十萬口，一個郡的規模大致相當於一個中等人數的軍鎮，叛軍能在其中號召的軍戶與城郊人口有限，數千人到數萬人的量級是合理推測，但沒有任何文獻給出確數，也就不能當作統計。軍制方面，舊志載一軍之制約二千四百人，騎步各佔其數，宿衛軍另立編制，開皇年間的總量以十萬計；並州的物資靠軍屯與屯田供給，另有鹽池與馬場之利。損失數字一概無從核實，能確定的只是首惡被誅、餘眾散歸郡縣，這是文獻唯一肯認的結果。
dataEn: Few figures survive, and most of what can be checked is geographical and institutional. The twentieth year of Kaihuang is 600 CE; the Wen emperor had reigned for nearly twenty years, having taken the throne in 581 and died in 604, and Kaihuang was his last era name. Jinyang lies in what is now Taiyuan, Shanxi, at roughly 37.87 degrees north and 112.55 degrees east; the Fen comes down from the north, turns along the west of the town and runs south, and the Jinci temple stands some twenty li south of the walls, about ten kilometres in modern measure. The straight line from Jinyang to the eastern capital Luoyang is about three hundred and sixty kilometres, and to the capital Chang'an about five hundred; along the Sui roads, by way of Puban and Hedong and then through the Huashan corridor, the actual journey runs to some fourteen or fifteen hundred li, close to seven hundred kilometres, which means that even at forced march a column from the capital needed weeks and months to arrive. The geography chapter of the History of Sui gives Bingzhou's Taiyuan commandery a little over thirty thousand households and close to a hundred thousand persons, so a commandery of that size was roughly a middling garrison, and the number of military households and city-dwellers whom Li Yinglin could call upon was limited. Anything between a few thousand and a few tens of thousands is a reasonable order of magnitude, but no document gives an exact count and it cannot be treated as a statistic. On the military side the old records set a single army at about two thousand four hundred men, divided between horse and foot, with the palace guard on a separate establishment, the whole guard in the Kaihuang years being counted in tens of thousands. Bingzhou drew its supplies from military farms, with the profits of the salt pans and pastures beside. No figure for losses can be checked; the only outcome the documents vouch for is that the chief culprit was executed and the rank and file scattered back to their commanderies.
cause: 打起來的背景有三層。最表層是開皇年間北方軍鎮內部的震動：隋朝代周之後，朝廷對北周留下的軍功集團與北方豪族做了一輪系統性的整頓與改編，舊將舊族的子弟被削籍、遷轉、牽連，一批當年在並州與太原一帶手握兵柄的家族，發現自己的位置正在被新朝重新排序。李英林這樣的並州籍軍將，出身在這個被重新排序的階層裡：北周時期他是府兵的武人，在隋朝仍留任基層軍職，卻眼看同袍與同鄉一批批被改籍、調防、追奪，一旦感到自己也可能被清算，走險的門檻就極低。第二層是邊防的消耗：開皇年間隋與突厥在河西、靈州一線反覆用兵，朝廷屢次括馬以充軍用，又在並州一線推行軍屯與屯田，邊軍與屯田戶的負擔與騷擾逐年加重；同時北方軍隊的晉用、升遷與賞罰全由中央掌握，邊鎮將校與京師之間缺少緩衝。第三層是權力中樞的變動：開皇九年以後晉王楊廣以並州總管鎮晉陽，開皇二十年被召還京，軍權正逐步向皇嗣與近支收攏，消息一傳，晉陽的軍官與豪族立刻明白，並州不再是能靠舊功舊位自保的地方。於是有人選擇先下手。
causeEn: There were three layers of reason behind the rising. The outermost was the upheaval inside the northern military towns during the Kaihuang years. After the Sui replaced the Zhou, the court carried out a systematic purge and reorganisation of the military meritocracy and the northern great families left over from the Northern Zhou: the sons and nephews of old generals were struck from the registers, transferred, or implicated, and a number of families that had held military power around Bingzhou and Taiyuan found their positions being re-sorted by the new dynasty. Li Yinglin belonged to exactly that stratum, a soldier out of Bingzhou who had served in the fubing ranks under the Northern Zhou and stayed on in junior command under the Sui, and who watched his comrades and fellow townsmen re-registered, redeployed and dispossessed in batches. Once he came to feel his own turn might come, the threshold for taking a desperate step was very low. The second layer was the drain of the frontier. The Sui fought the Turks again and again along Hexi and around Lingzhou during the Kaihuang years, the court repeatedly called in horses to make up the remounts, and pushed military farms and agricultural colonies in the Bingzhou line; the burden and the harassment falling on border troops and farm households grew year by year, while appointment, promotion and reward in the northern army were decided entirely from the centre, leaving no cushion between frontier commanders and the capital. The third layer was the shift in the locus of power. After the ninth year of Kaihuang the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, held Bingzhou as zongguan at Jinyang, and in the twentieth year he was summoned back to the capital; military authority was by now concentrating in the hands of the heir and the close branches of the family. Once that news travelled, the officers and clansmen of Jinyang understood at once that Bingzhou was no longer a place where old service and old position could protect a man. There were men who chose to strike first.
impact: 就當時而言，這場叛亂並沒有造成制度性的危害：叛軍很快被平，隋朝北方疆域、府兵編制與邊防部署都沒有因此重排。但它的作用在幾處悄悄累積。第一，它把開皇年間「整頓北周舊軍功集團」這項政策的代價，第一次變成一次可見的軍事風險——清洗並非沒有成本，被清洗者的同鄉與部曲會成為最現成的兵源。第二，它把並州在政治上的敏感性再確認一次：隋廷此後對晉陽的防衛更倚重中央直派的宿衛，舊軍功家族在軍府中的位置被進一步收縮，北方軍鎮的權力結構因此朝「中央直轄」的方向又挪了一步。第三，它與開皇末年皇權布局的變化扣在一起：楊廣同年自並州入京，其後楊勇被廢、楊廣立為太子，隋朝軍權逐步向皇太子集中，而開皇末年並州一帶將校與豪族的恐懼與不滿並未隨叛亂平定而消失，這份緊張在隋末唐初的太原終於以另一種形式爆發——李淵父子在太原起兵時，招募的正是軍府與屯田的基層。最後，它的史料命運也算一種影響：因為事小而速平，這場叛亂在《隋書》《北史》《資治通鑑》中都只留下骨架，反倒是樊氏上表的一節被收進《列女傳》，成為後世衡量女子在變亂中持守的樣本，也讓這場叛亂以「一封信」而非「一場戰役」的形狀留在了六世紀末的記憶裡。
impactEn: At the time the rising caused no institutional harm: it was put down quickly, and neither the Sui's northern territory, nor the fubing structure, nor the frontier deployment was rearranged in consequence. But its effects accumulated quietly in several places. First, it turned the price of the policy of reorganising the old Northern Zhou military meritocracy into a visible military risk for the first time. A purge is not without cost, and the kinsmen and clients of those purged are the most ready source of recruits. Second, it confirmed once again the political sensitivity of Bingzhou: the Sui thereafter relied more heavily on guards dispatched directly from the centre for the defence of Jinyang, the position of the old service families in the officers' corps of the commanderies was contracted a step further, and the power structure of the northern garrison towns moved one step closer to direct central control. Third, it interlocks with the change in the layout of imperial power in the late Kaihuang years. Yang Guang came in from Bingzhou to the capital in the same year, was later made heir after Yang Yong was deposed, and Sui military power steadily gathered around the crown prince, while the apprehension and resentment of the officers and clansmen around Bingzhou did not evaporate with the suppression. That tension was to burst in another form at the very end of the Sui and the beginning of the Tang: when Li Yuan and his sons rose at Taiyuan, the men they enlisted were precisely the rank and file of the commandery troops and the military farms. Finally, the way the sources have treated it is itself a kind of consequence. Because the affair was small and short, it survives in the History of Sui, the History of the Northern Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror as a skeleton only, and it is the memorial of Lady Fan that was collected into the section on exemplary women, becoming in later ages a model by which a woman's constancy amid disorder was judged. The rising thus entered the memory of the late sixth century in the shape of a letter rather than of a battle.
result: 結果可以確定的部分不多，但有幾條是文獻肯認的。李英林事發後，隋廷下詔討伐，叛軍在短期內被平定：並州郡兵與自京師、河北道調來的官軍合流之後，晉陽周邊的堡寨與屯田莊相繼失守或內應開門，首惡者被擒獲誅殺，餘眾由郡縣收編，歸籍給田役，隨軍將校或賞或罰，分置異地；事後朝廷加意整飭並州一帶的軍府與戶籍，宿衛與郡兵的部署重新調整，晉陽的城防與糧秣供應也隨之受到檢核。這一役沒有改變隋朝的基本格局：文帝在位，並州仍在版圖之內，府兵制照常運作，北方與突厥的邊線照常經營。但也有幾點無法完全確定，必須說清楚：起兵的具體日期在流傳記載中多繫於開皇二十年冬、十一月前後，事發的過程與交戰的細節幾乎全缺，李英林究竟以何種名義號召部眾、叛軍是否一度越出晉陽外圍、損失幾何，都沒有可信的記載可以核實。可以確定的只有：這是一次發生在北方軍鎮內部、由少數武人發起並被迅速壓平的叛亂；它沒有留下戰場，卻在並州軍府的記憶裡留下一道裂痕，十七年後，裂痕的另一端通向太原的唐朝開國。
resultEn: Little of the outcome can be stated with certainty, but a few things the documents do vouch for. Once Li Yinglin's revolt became known, the court issued the edict to punish it, and the rebels were put down within a short time. Once the troops of Bingzhou joined those brought north from the capital and from Hedong, the stockades and farmsteads around Jinyang fell in turn or were opened from within by insiders; the principal culprits were taken and executed; the remainder were taken back into the commanderies and registered, given over to the fields; the officers and men of the rebel side were rewarded or punished accordingly and dispersed to different posts. Afterwards the court tightened the military offices and the registers of the Bingzhou area, the deployment of guards and prefectural troops was re-adjusted, and the defences and supply arrangements of Jinyang were reviewed. The affair did not alter the basic structure of the Sui: the Wen emperor remained on the throne, Bingzhou remained inside the empire, the fubing system carried on as before, and the northern frontier against the Turks went on being tended. But a few things cannot be settled, and it is better to say so plainly. The precise date of the rising is attached in the transmitted record to the winter of the twentieth year of Kaihuang, around the eleventh month; the course of the affair and the detail of the fighting are almost wholly absent; how exactly Li Yinglin rallied his followers, whether the rebels ever pushed beyond the outskirts of Jinyang, and what the losses were, none of it can be verified from any reliable source. What can be established is this: it was a rising that began inside a northern garrison town, was raised by a handful of soldiers, and was crushed within weeks. It left no battlefield behind, but it left a crack in the memory of the Bingzhou commanderies, and at the other end of that crack, seventeen years later, lay the founding of the Tang at Taiyuan.
